passages.title: Learning the guitar at forty
passages.text:
When I was a child, I always wanted to learn the guitar, but my parents couldn't afford lessons. Two years ago, on my fortieth birthday, I finally bought one and tried to teach (1) ______ by watching videos online.

The beginning was hard. My fingers hurt quite (2) ______ lot, and they weren't strong (3) ______ to press the strings down properly. After a month I nearly gave (4) ______ playing.

Then my daughter found me a teacher, Sara, and everything changed. She explained that the pain happens to all beginners and that the skin gets harder with practice. Apart (5) ______ the technique, she has taught me to read music and to play in a band with other adult learners, which is the best part of my week.

I now try to practise for twenty minutes every evening (6) ______ I am working late. Next month our music school is having a concert, and I am going to play in front of an audience for the first time. I'm nervous, but also very excited.

questions.question: Gap (1): I finally bought one and tried to teach ____ by watching videos online.
questions.explanation: The subject 'I' is also the person who learns, so the verb 'teach' needs the reflexive pronoun 'myself' ('teach myself' = learn without a teacher). 'Me' is not correct when the object is the same person as the subject.

questions.question: Gap (2): My fingers hurt quite ____ lot.
questions.explanation: 'Quite a lot' is a fixed expression meaning 'very much'. 'Lot' needs the article 'a' here; 'quite the lot' or 'quite lot' are not correct.

questions.question: Gap (3): They weren't strong ____ to press the strings down properly.
questions.explanation: 'Adjective + enough + to-infinitive' says whether something has the necessary quality: the fingers did not have the strength needed. 'Enough' comes after the adjective ('strong enough'); 'too' and 'very' go before it.

questions.question: Gap (4): After a month I nearly gave ____ playing.
questions.explanation: 'Give up + -ing' is a phrasal verb meaning 'stop doing something'. The writer found it hard and almost stopped. 'Gave in' is not followed by an -ing form, and 'gave away' needs an object like 'the guitar'.

questions.question: Gap (5): Apart ____ the technique, she has taught me to read music and to play in a band.
questions.explanation: 'Apart from' means 'as well as / in addition to'. 'Apart' is always followed by 'from' in this expression.

questions.question: Gap (6): I now try to practise for twenty minutes every evening ____ I am working late.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'except if': the writer practises every evening, but not on the evenings when they work late. 'If' or 'when' would mean the opposite (practising only on those late evenings).
